intended_object: The row-superstandard standard Young tableau of a Young diagram μ: the standard tableau labelling the cells in reading order (row by row, left to right). Inferred from the docstring and module doc (Fulton, Young Tableaux §1.1).
explanation: In this library a tableau is a bijection from μ.cells to Fin μ.card, so labels are 0-indexed; that is a library-wide convention. The definition sends cell (i,j) to readingIndex μ (i,j) = (number of cells in rows 0..i-1) + j, which is exactly the cell's position in reading order. It proves this map injective via eq_of_readingIndex_eq; injectivity plus equal cardinalities gives a bijection. Labels strictly increase along rows, since the reading index grows with the column within a fixed row. They strictly increase down columns, since every cell of μ in an earlier row has a smaller reading index than any cell in a later row. This is the row-superstandard tableau, and the empty diagram is handled correctly. The notion is specific to Young diagrams, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has semistandard Young tableaux but no standard Young tableaux and no superstandard tableau, so there is no counterpart.
